rationale: The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (cache dependency downloads) applies to this Rust workflow: every job (test, no-std-build-test, lint, miri) repeatedly fetches crates from crates.io with no existing dependency cache, so repeated dependency fetching is measurable and cache inputs can be keyed on Cargo.lock plus runner OS. The pattern's preconditions are met and there are no contraindications (no mutable/untrusted cached content, no equivalent cache already present). I added actions/cache@v4 for ~/.cargo/registry and ~/.cargo/git before the cargo commands in each job, keyed by hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') with a restore-key prefix for partial matches. This avoids re-downloading dependencies on warm runs while preserving all build and test coverage: no steps, features, targets, toolchains, or required checks are removed or changed. It uses only the standard GitHub Actions cache service, adds no secrets, privileged actions, publishing/deployment, or new network access beyond cache storage/retrieval.
